{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-az-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"0492b70c8a184d53176533b16c87cfd425dff7ad609cd3808a4a633858cea1b4","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-az-class-d:lineage:51","source_registry_sha256":"6dbbc2d22fea619728bdb90038a4aedf3afc07eab652b3f97027c9c69aaadaf4","source_liveness_sha256":"1c5753487760cbe2044d84b5696121c7181af61815b598d89d5ce158abf5fe43"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C","chunk_id":"C.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Railroad crossing cautions, highway route markers and mile posts, work zones, work-zone devices and fines, flaggers, and pavement markings","heading":"C — The last railroad crossing cautions, route markers and mile posts, work-zone hazards and doubled fines, flaggers and work-zone devices, and what yellow and white pavement markings, lane arrows and painted curbs mean","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — The last railroad crossing cautions, route markers and mile posts, work-zone hazards and doubled fines, flaggers and work-zone devices, and what yellow and white pavement markings, lane arrows and painted curbs mean
Knowledge domain: the closing railroad crossing cautions, how Arizona route markers and mile posts help you report where you are, why work zones are dangerous and what their devices and flaggers tell you, when work-zone fines are doubled, and how to read yellow and white lines, lane arrows, bicycle symbols and painted curbs.

FACT_ID: sec12-F01 | anchor: A01
Never try to race a train or any other on-track equipment to a crossing. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F02 | anchor: A01
Expect buses and gasoline tankers to stop at railroad crossings, because those vehicles are required to stop there. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F03 | anchor: A01
When driving at night, watch for railroad crossing warning signs that may not be lit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F04 | anchor: A01
Highway guide signs include route markers for interstate routes, national routes and state routes. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F05 | anchor: A01
Arizona is one of only a few states that has mileage markers on every state highway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F06 | anchor: A01
Arizona mile posts stand 2 feet off the right shoulder of the highway. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F07 | anchor: A01
Arizona mile posts are placed about 1 mile apart. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F08 | anchor: A01
A nearby mile post lets you tell others where you are after a crash, a mechanical problem or running out of gas. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F09 | anchor: A01
If you have to stop on a highway, note which route you are on and roughly how far you are from a mile post. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F10 | anchor: A01
A work zone can be a long-term project with permanent signs or a temporary site with portable signs that stays up for only a few hours. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F11 | anchor: A01
Typical work-zone crashes are rear-end collisions from drivers going too fast, collisions with fixed objects, and vehicles striking the people working there. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F12 | anchor: A01
In a work zone, stay on high alert and be ready to slow or stop suddenly for changing conditions, including a change in the road surface. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F13 | anchor: A01
Workers and construction vehicles may be right beside the travel lanes or may enter them at any point in the work zone. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F14 | anchor: A01
The alerting and controlling devices used in construction and maintenance areas protect highway workers as well as guiding drivers and pedestrians. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F15 | anchor: A01
Orange is the basic color of the warning devices used in road construction and maintenance areas. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F16 | anchor: A01
At every construction site you must drive slowly, stay especially alert and obey the posted speed limit. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0043]

FACT_ID: sec12-F17 | anchor: A02
A work-zone speed limit protects the workers doing the job as well as the drivers passing through. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F18 | anchor: A02
When work-zone signs are posted, the fine for a speeding violation there is doubled. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F19 | anchor: A02
Flaggers are used in road work zones to stop traffic, slow it down or guide it safely through. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F20 | anchor: A02
Flaggers wear orange vests or jackets and direct traffic with red flags or stop and slow panels. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F21 | anchor: A02
Construction and maintenance signs warn drivers of possible danger in or near a work area. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F22 | anchor: A02
Most of the signs used in highway and street work areas are diamond-shaped. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F23 | anchor: A02
Flashing arrow panels are used both day and night to warn you early that you must move left or right into another lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F24 | anchor: A02
When you see a flashing arrow panel, slow down and get ready to merge in the direction the arrow points. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F25 | anchor: A02
Electronic message signs on some roads give advance warning of construction zones, special traffic directions, road closures or weather conditions. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F26 | anchor: A02
Cones, drums and barricades alert you and guide you safely through a work area, and at night they may carry warning lights. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F27 | anchor: A02
Pavement markings guide and warn drivers and also regulate traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0044]

FACT_ID: sec12-F28 | anchor: A03
Pavement markings are either yellow or white, they can be combined, and each combination carries its own meaning. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F29 | anchor: A03
Yellow center lines tell you that traffic on the road flows in both directions. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F30 | anchor: A03
White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and also mark the road edge, stop lines and pedestrian crosswalks. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F31 | anchor: A03
A broken yellow line lets you pass on the left when the road is clear, but because you face oncoming traffic you must pass with extreme caution. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F32 | anchor: A03
Where a broken yellow line runs beside a solid yellow line, passing is allowed in only one direction. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F33 | anchor: A03
If the broken yellow line is on your side, you may pass once the road ahead is clear. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F34 | anchor: A03
Passing is not allowed when the solid yellow line is the one nearest your lane. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F35 | anchor: A03
Double solid yellow lines ban passing in both directions, and you may cross them only to make a left turn. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F36 | anchor: A03
Broken white lines separate lanes going the same way and may be crossed with caution after you signal your lane change. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F37 | anchor: A03
Solid white lines mark turn lanes and keep drivers from changing lanes near intersections. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F38 | anchor: A03
If your lane shows a curved arrow with the word ONLY, you must turn the way the arrow points. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F39 | anchor: A03
If your lane shows both a curved arrow and a straight arrow, you may either turn that way or go straight. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F40 | anchor: A03
A bicycle painted on the road warns that bicyclists may be present, so drive with caution. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

FACT_ID: sec12-F41 | anchor: A03
A painted curb means special rules apply if you want to park there, and each curb color has its own meaning. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0045]

Misconceptions: a broken yellow line allows passing but still puts you in the lane of oncoming traffic, so it is not a casual lane change; double solid yellow lines may be crossed only to turn left, never to pass; doubled work-zone fines are tied to posted signs; a curved arrow without the word ONLY does not force a turn when a straight arrow is also painted.
Mnemonics: Yellow divides opposite directions, white divides the same direction; broken means you may cross with care, solid means stay put.
Glossary: mile post means a roadside reference marker on Arizona state highways used to report your location; flagger means a work-zone worker in orange who directs traffic with a flag or a stop and slow panel; flashing arrow panel means a lighted arrow board telling you to merge; regulate means to control traffic by rule.
Dynamic facts: work-zone fine rules are statutory and can be amended, and work-zone layouts, electronic message sign content and portable signs change with each project.
